free_tier.stated: 5,242,880,000 bytes (~5 GB) per package zip — documented as a soft limit that staff will raise on request; server default in source is REPOSITORY_MAX_PACKAGE_SIZE_MB=500. No per-team total quota; the only total cap is a global server-wide REPOSITORY_MAX_PACKAGE_TOTAL_SIZE_GB=1000.

egress.terms: Free and CDN-fronted: download URLs 302 to ccdn.thunderstore.io with `Cache-Control: max-age=2678400`, `Server: cloudflare`, no auth.

tooling: Package upload via multipart POST to /api/experimental/submission/upload/ (thunderstore-cli, tcli); metadata read via /api/experimental/package/. No rclone backend, CLI wrapper exists: github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli.
chaining: Unlimited packages x 5 GB each. Team is the ownership unit, one user can create many teams; nothing in the source caps packages per team. 20 packages = 100 GB, 200 = 1 TB, all on a free account.
limits_note: 5 GB/zip soft cap; package must be a valid zip with manifest.json + icon.png 256x256 + README.md at root; per-game community listing required; uploads land in a moderation queue; source shows a global 1000 GB server cap shared by the whole platform (not per-user) which would reject new uploads if ever hit.
reliability_note: Packages surviving as 'mods' for a real game community; orphaned/garbage packages are routinely delisted, which deletes files.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'Currently there's a maximum package size limit of 5 242 880 000 bytes (or roughly 5 GB), but this is a soft-limit and can be increased if needed'
